subject: Renewal + sprint bundle conversion options
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jill Tan <jill.tan@averylabs.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + sprint bundle conversion options

Hi Jill —

Congrats again on the pilot results last quarter. As we look toward your August 15 renewal, a couple of questions came up from your team about mid-contract growth and whether we can convert your short-term sprint credit purchases into a longer-term bundle without losing the pacing flexibility.

Quick summary of what we can do and what I need from you: 
- Option A: Convert the existing sprint credits into a 12-month bundle (co-term with the renewal) with a 10% uplift discount on committed units if Avery commits to a minimum reserved token level (details attached). This preserves current unit economics for typical spike patterns and gives you priority capacity.
- Option B: Keep sprint credits as-is but add an on-demand top-up band with a capped surge rate and a 5% discount on converted volume. No co-term required.
- Option C: Hybrid — convert 60% of sprint credits into an annualized pool and leave 40% as flexible sprint credits; discount ~7% on converted portion.

Can you confirm which direction procurement prefers and whether they need a sample invoice format or PO language? Naomi, looping you in for any billing questions.

I attached a short worksheet that models the three options against the usage pattern you shared. Happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow to walk through numbers.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0122

Attachment: sprint-bundle-pricing-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet — pricing scenarios)

From: Jill Tan <jill.tan@averylabs.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@averylabs.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + sprint bundle conversion options

Thanks, Karthik — appreciate the clear options. Procurement is leaning toward a conversion rather than leaving credits as bursts; they want predictable monthly cost with the ability to absorb a two-week spike each quarter. A few clarifying asks: 
1) If we convert and co-term, can you preserve existing surge caps for uncommitted usage?
2) What’s the minimum reserved token threshold to hit the 10% uplift discount in Option A?
3) We need sample PO language and a line-item split for billing (annualized bundle vs sprint remainder).

I’m tied up all day Monday — can we do a call Tuesday morning PT?

—Jill
Director, Cloud Integrations
Avery Labs
jill.tan@averylabs.ai

> 
> Congrats again on the pilot results last quarter...

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Jill Tan <jill.tan@averylabs.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Jul 2027 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + sprint bundle conversion options — pricing scenarios attached

Hi Jill — looping in the pricing worksheet inline and attaching the full spreadsheet. Short answers up front: 
- Surge caps: yes, we can preserve the current burst cap for uncommitted usage at the same per-token overage rate you have today. We’ll mark that as an invoice line: "On-demand surge (capped)" so procurement can see it clearly.
- Minimum reserved threshold for 10% uplift: 120M reserved inference tokens over 12 months (averaged ~10M / month). If you commit to that threshold we can extend the 10% uplift on the converted units; lower commitments qualify for the tiered discounts in the attachment.
- PO wording: see the sample line below and the attached PDF for a formatted snippet.

Sample invoice line-item split (example):
- Annualized Sprint Bundle (committed) — 120,000,000 tokens — $X,XXX,XXX — discounted 10%
- Flexible Sprint Credits (on-demand pool) — 40,000,000 tokens — $XXX,XXX — surge cap applies
- On-demand surge (metered above caps) — $/token (capped monthly at Y%)

I attached: sprint-bundle-pricing-v2.xlsx (detailed tiers), co-term-illustration.pdf (sample PO lines).

If that looks good we can prepare a co-term amendment and a DocuSign ready exhibit for signature. Karthik — I put a recommended revenue recognition note for finance on tab 3 (NA) so legal/procurement can review.

Cheers,
Priyom
Senior Pricing Analyst, Redwood Inference
priom_das@redwood.com

> On Fri, Jul 02, 2027 at 11:07 AM Jill Tan <jill.tan@averylabs.ai> wrote:
> > Thanks, Karthik — appreciate the clear options...

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jill Tan <jill.tan@averylabs.ai>, procurement@averylabs.ai
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Jul 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + sprint bundle conversion options — next steps

Jill / procurement team —

Thanks for the quick read. To make the Tuesday call productive, proposed agenda: 
1) Confirm target reserved threshold (we recommend 120M tokens for the 10% uplift).
2) Run through the attached invoice split and PO snippet so procurement can confirm language.
3) Discuss co-term amendment timeline (we can have a DocuSign exhibit ready within 48 hours once you sign off on threshold).

As a commercial sweetener to help with approval cycles, we can offer a 60-day limited-time credit of $25k applied to the first invoice if Avery signs the co-term conversion (this is one-time and requires agreement on the 120M threshold). If procurement prefers a phased approach, we can also stage the commitment (60/40 in months 1–6 / 7–12) with prorated discounts.

Please confirm Tuesday 10:00 AM PT or propose another slot. I’ll bring Naomi for billing questions and Priyom for pricing specifics.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment list: sprint-bundle-pricing-v2.xlsx, co-term-illustration.pdf
